signals.learning_signal: On decide/guarantee signatures with a buried-but-supplied option (rescue base rate present in the data but unflagged), branch completeness must run BEFORE selection: a tree with an unpriced failure branch overstates the root by 11 (62 vs 73) and the p* threshold by 0.09 (0.56 vs 0.474); the opportunity-cost framing ('what does abandoning forgo?') is the cheapest in-frame detector of a hidden branch.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the P3 branch-completeness gate as a standing pre-DO contract on decision-tree signatures (it converts the v5 review-repair into in-frame pricing); pair m023 opportunity-cost as the hidden-branch detector in HOW; add 'renegotiation floor at the indifference threshold' as a packet line whenever a firm outside offer stands (the $170M threshold is an action item, not a footnote).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline applied the style purely and failed on cue — exhaustive forgone-alternative enumeration with no stop condition cycled re-pricing passes past all three 14-day windows (all offers forgone, counteroffer withdrawn) and monetized the non-fungible. The non-routed v5 AI already won (2.0/5.0) by improvising the band -> VOI~0 -> rule chain, but the routed run makes the escape structural: m088 pre-commitment leads (the re-analysis loop is the temptation the pass pre-binds against; the 48h commit is a Ulysses contract), m023 runs as protective context with its known trap gate-checked (its own Step-7 insight — 'the best forgone alternative is the decision itself' — operationalized in-frame, not discovered at REVIEW), m031 bounds the analysis to one discriminating pass with a falsifier, and tempo mode (P2) commits at DO.
signals.learning_signal: On near-tie signatures with hard windows, the opportunity-cost discipline must be applied against itself: when the error band makes ranking differences noise, the costliest forgone alternative is the decision itself, so the stop condition (VOI ~ 0) and the commitment mechanism (pre-stated tie-breaker + binding deadline) ARE the deliverable, not another decimal place; the registry's own weakness ('counting everything can freeze action') is the routing flag that a protective gate (R2) must pair with the style — on NEG signatures the router should move top-1 away from the trap style toward a commitment mechanism (m088), holding the negative split at >= 90% AI wins.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m088 pre-commitment as the primary route for hard-window near-ties (the loop is a temptation, not a computation), with m023 as gate-checked context rather than lead; install 'time-box enumeration to one pass with explicit error bands; commit inside the window on a pre-stated tie-breaker' as a standing contract; log every near-tie where re-pricing cycled as a curriculum item — tempo mode (P2) already enforces the commit at DO, so the loop-catastrophe is now structurally unreachable.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline made the $1.5M forgone-alternative comparison the constitutive frame in-frame (sunk $370K excluded, verdict B with Elena, all rubric items) while the non-routed v5 AI computed the same numbers but buried the comparator — the opportunity-cost spine was reached only at REVIEW, status APPROXIMATED, and it lost 5.0/4.0 on the style's home turf. The routed run installs m023 as a first-class pass with an explicit completion contract (best-forgone-alternative valued explicitly, sunk-cost stripped, resource-discipline check), so the comparator is the spine of HOW, not a REVIEW discovery; m044 flags the board chair as interested party (the sunk-cost pitch is motivated, not just fallacious); m003 and m019 gates add >=6 ranked failure categories and enumerated exploit vectors with quantified exposure in-frame; P1/P3 run before selection; verdict flips to an AI narrow edge on breadth.
signals.learning_signal: On decide/maximize signatures with sunk spend and a scarce-resource fork, computing the opportunity cost is necessary but not sufficient: the frame that defines the decision ('what does this choice forgo, and does the forgone beat it?') must LEAD the pass, or the math is right and the reasoning still loses on the style's home turf; P1 interested-party provenance upgrades 'the chair's fallacy' from a refutation target into the first audit (who benefits is a first-class input property), and the $1.5M gap is a decision line, not a supporting calculation.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m023 opportunity-cost as a contract pass (explicit best-forgone-alternative statement + sunk-cost strip + resource-discipline check) on any scarce-resource-fork + sunk-spend signature; pair with m044 stakeholder when an interested party champions sunk work; report the opportunity-cost gap as a packet line (the $1.5M is the price of 'finishing what we started') so the verdict IS the comparison — this converts the v5 REVIEW-repair into in-frame reasoning and flips the POS-01 loss.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style human baseline amplified the hindsight anchor on cue — the 80-year-old test ratified the $376 purchase after a 47x run as a second chance and endorsed the all-in $53K incl. margin (2.0/5.0), with base rates (70% past-winner reversal), valuation (P/E 85 vs 26), insider sales, and the ~40% margin-call ruin path excluded from the frame; its honest Step-6 self-diagnosis arrives after the endorsement. The non-routed v5 AI already won 5.0 by improvising the 2013≠2026 decision-split. The routed run makes the escape structural: the router's NEG dual-route (confident=no → m064 + m089 first-class, trap style m024 out of top-3) plus the m007 ruin screen (R3) — the hindsight-contamination guard and anchor audit (P1: the 2013 $8 buy is not a purchasable 2026 decision; family group chat is pressure, not evidence) are contracts in-frame, the margin veto is a ruin-screen conclusion (forced realized sale at the bottom, negative-Kelly at P/E 85), and the m011 loop scan exposes the miss-recurrence mechanism so the auto-invest process fix treats the real wound.
signals.learning_signal: The 80-year-old test is an amplifier of whatever regret is currently loudest, not a purifier: fed a vivid recent miss it returns an emotionally biased, hindsight-contaminated concentrated bet exactly where sober expected value (base rates, valuation, explicit ruin path) wins. On decide/maximize signatures with a recent-miss anchor, routing must move top-1 AWAY from the trap style (NEG metric, held here: m024 out of top-3 on its own negative case), run dual passes on ambiguity, and make the ruin screen (R3) mandatory — margin/leverage must never amplify a regret-motivated position; the guard clause (regret over decision quality, not outcome; anchor decision ≠ available decision stated before any allocation math) and the recurrence-mechanism fix (auto-invest as the cheap decisive experiment) are the deliverables, not another price forecast.
signals.suggested_improvement: Hold the m024 contract's hindsight-contamination clause on ANY signature containing a recent-miss anchor: restate the decision in its current-time form and check anchor availability ('is the regretted decision still purchasable?') before regret reasoning may set an allocation; cap emotional evidence when the anchor is unavailable and require base rates, valuation, and an explicit worst-case/ruin-path calculation on the record; hard-rule that margin may not enter a regret-motivated position without an independent base-rate justification; on ambiguous NEG signatures keep dual-route (top-2 passes + synthesis) with m007 mandatory — this holds the NEG split at >= 90% AI wins and converts the v5 improvised escape into a structural one.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline made the 80-year-old projection the spine in-frame — performed concretely and argued from Elena's own documents (8 years of letters, mentor testimony, marketability test), it bracketed the washed-out EV in one move and pre-eliminated 'wait for more certainty' before it existed (5.0/4.0 human). The non-routed v5 AI reached the same leap-with-bounded-commitment but promoted the omission>commission asymmetry to primary status only at selection and killed its delay hedge only at verification — an ordering loss the v5 AAR itself conceded. The routed run installs m024 as a first-class pass with an explicit contract (regret-at-80 performed concretely, hindsight guard — regret over decision quality not outcome, long-horizon tiebreaker on the EV wash, opportunity-cost cross-check of stay/delay), so the projection is the spine of HOW: the delay alternative is pre-eliminated by the 60-day clock inside the regret ranking, the EV is bracketed in-frame at WHY (no wash-burn, no hedge the clock kills); m039 barbell context, m011 loop scan, m003's 7 ranked failure categories (incl. durable-omission), and m007's floor/Kelly/provenance ruin screen add breadth; verdict flips to an AI narrow edge.
signals.learning_signal: On decide/high_stakes signatures where EV is a deliberate wash and a one-shot clock binds, the long-horizon regret test must LEAD the pass, not arbitrate at selection: the frame's spine is the 80-year-old projection run before alternative generation, with an explicit hindsight-contamination guard so the failure branch stays priced-in (regret on decision quality, not outcome), an EV-bracket conclusion ('wash or decisive') so the test is named as the tiebreaker, and an opportunity-cost cross-check that makes the status-quo's cost visible in-frame. Late-promoted regret evidence is fragile — it drifts to 'stay' under unfavorable EV and manufactures certainty-chasing hedges a 60-day clock makes fatal; 'wait for more certainty' must be pre-eliminated by the calendar inside the regret ranking, not killed at verification.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the m024 first-class pass contract on long-horizon commitment forks (career, business bets, relocations): (1) perform the horizon projection concretely before generation, sourced from the decider's OWN documented values (letters, journals, mentor testimony), not generic risk preference; (2) state the hindsight guard (regret over decision quality, not outcome) so failure branches are priced in, not feared out; (3) require the EV pass to conclude 'wash or decisive' and name the test as the tiebreaker on a wash; (4) pre-eliminate delay/defer alternatives on one-shot clocks by an explicit clock-kill line; (5) pair with m003 (ranked failure categories incl. durable-omission) and m007 (floor/no-ruin) on high_stakes — this converts the v5 ordering loss into an in-frame win.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline triggered the registry's registered weakness on cue — it priced the pilot's information (+$20M) and priced the cost of exercising the option at zero, computing staged EV at +$74M (erosion unpriced; true +$39M) and recommending a staged path worth $15M less than committing now. The routed run's m064 first-class pass surfaced the information-vs-contract value conflict and its resolution-algorithm weakness gate forced the arithmetic: net option value 20−50 = −$30M made decisive; the m003 inversion gate ranked 'stage anyway / let the deadline decide' as the top failure category (likely × severe) before DO; the m007 screen priced the full distribution (70% +$120M / 30% −$100M vs staged −$10M floor) and the m019 gate quantified the $50M contract exposure and the false-vs-true staged EV gap (−$35M). The wait was priced as a strike, not waved through.
signals.learning_signal: The overstaging failure mode is exercised exactly when the cost of the wait is priced at zero: any stage that delays a dated, contested decision must be charged its full exercise cost (forgone contract, eroded payoff) against the information it buys — net option value = isolated information value − wait cost; when net < 0, commit now and take only zero-schedule information (parallel probes, non-delaying kill options). A style's known failure mode is best gated by pairing the pass with inversion (rank 'stage anyway' and 'let the deadline decide' as top failure categories) and with ruin/distribution screens that price the erosion branch, so the trap is priced as a branch rather than dodged.
signals.suggested_improvement: Make 'exercise-cost of the wait' a mandatory line of the option-structure completion contract (the router's confident single-route here was m064, whose resolution-algorithm weakness happened to force the netting — the option pass itself should carry the price-the-wait check so it never needs a rescuer); pair m025 with m003 inversion as its protective gate whenever deadline/adversarial appear in the signature (the 'stage anyway' and 'let the deadline decide' categories first); retain tempo mode (P2) so commit-at-DO fires inside the contract window and the closed-scope fast path compresses the fully-specified case.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline performed the full option-theoretic discipline at first sight (irreversibility named first, option value 50−20=+30 explicit, kill criteria pre-committed, max-payable $45M, no redundant second stage, growth option priced) — moves the v5 non-routed AI only recovered in its REVIEW AAR (break-even and the growth option arrived post-hoc). The routed run's m025 completion contract promoted all of these to first-class HOW outputs, matching the baseline's depth, while the m019 gate (adversarial context is internal here — gate-gaming, qualification leverage) added quantified per-vector exposure and independent-verification counters the human baseline does not price, and the m044 dual pass added second-order reactions (Meridian qualification leverage, COGS-threshold Goodhart). Residual shared gap: independent verification of pilot data is assumed available, not contracted.
signals.learning_signal: On irreversible-capital decisions (decide/estimate/maximize + adversarial), the signature discipline is option pricing, not EV: name irreversibility first (single-purpose capital, resale ≈ 0), decompose the stage's value as expected-dead-money-avoided p(failure)×K minus total stage cost (pilot + schedule), state the max-payable stage cost (staging loses when total stage cost ≥ p(failure)×K) as a negotiation ceiling, pre-commit numeric kill criteria BEFORE spending, refuse stages with ≈0 marginal information, and price growth options from the same information. In adversarial context without a market clock, the adversary is internal (teams paid to game thresholds or to overstage) — the adversary gate must enumerate those vectors and pair each with a counter (independent verification, contracted scope).
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m025 as the confident-route first-class pass on this signature with the option-structure completion contract (irreversibility check, information bought per stage, kill criteria, max-payable, no-overstage, growth option) — it converts the v5 REVIEW-recovery pattern (break-even, growth option found in the AAR) into first-class output; keep m019 as the standing R3 gate for adversarial capital decisions with threshold-gaming as an explicit vector and independent-verification as its counter; keep the m044 dual pass on decide/maximize signatures with organizational stakeholders (qualification leverage, build-team incentives).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure analogical style was trapped by a partially-true analogy — it built a rich surface mapping, let the genuine placement sub-correspondence (Pilot A 40%) license wholesale transfer, re-framed the extended-pilot mechanism (11% contradictory local decisions) as adaptation noise plus self-healing, and recommended deleting consensus on a twice-fined path. The routed dual-route (m003 inversion + m018 steel-manning; m026 held out of top-3) produced the bounded transfer: steel-manning credited the placement correspondence (the baseline's one true insight), inversion's failure tree named the missing agreement relation as the disqualifier, and the m019 context priced the 11% against the consensus baseline — the baseline-risk comparison the non-routed v5 run left unquantified.
signals.learning_signal: On pattern-transfer evaluation tasks the router correctly holds the trap style out of top-3; the winning configuration is inversion (failure-tree naming the missing load-bearing relation) + steel-manning (strongest bounded version) synthesized, with embedded pilot mechanisms treated as first-class falsifiers (mechanism-level, not outcome-rate) and a baseline-risk comparison (11% vs the consensus path's near-zero historical inconsistency).
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m026 hold-out routing on signatures with a transferred-pattern + pilot-data combination; install baseline-risk comparison as a standing m019-context output on proposal-evaluation cases; require the mapping-boundary statement in the decision packet (never transfer beyond the screened relation; the boundary name is inspectable). Cross-link: the POS signal installs the generative half of analogical competence, this signal the evaluative half — both should stay in the KB as the m026 pair.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline mapped and transferred superbly (fortress siege / radiation beams → 4-fan convergence, canopy -1.2 C) and is essentially the gold standard on its home turf; its marginal gaps are that it never verifies the transferred relations actually hold in the source before transfer, covers failure only as a fallback paragraph, and makes no tempo commit. The routed pass closed each: the m026 completion contract added source-guarantee verification (beams genuinely sum at the focus; tissue along each beam stays below harm), the m003 inversion gate produced >=6 ranked failure categories (fan failure, cold forecast, mis-aim) with failure-branch pricing, and tempo mode committed the 4-fan plan at DO with a 5th/6th-fan standby. Outcome vs the v5 regression: the non-routed v5 AI never generated the convergent class and certified a 60-75% loss as APPROXIMATED; the routed run saves the crop with the baseline's own numbers.
signals.learning_signal: On guarantee+deadline signatures with a fixed evidence set, the m026 pass wins when its completion contract includes source-verification (verify the transferred relations hold in the source, check the analogy's guarantees before transfer) and it is paired with the m003 inversion gate and a tempo commit; the mapping table alone ties the baseline, the contract + gate edge it.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the m026 completion contract exactly as installed (source-guarantee verification is the differentiator, not the correspondence count); maintain the m003 pairing on guarantee goals (R4) and tempo mode on deadline context (P2); keep the closed-scope fast path for fully-specified signatures so the pass compresses after generation. Regression evidence: the routed run alone flips m026-POS-01 from a clear loss (3.4) to a narrow win over the baseline.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline ran a genuine, full-cycle engagement whose prototype tests showed 10/12 resident delight and zero movement in the wait arithmetic — the constraint (Car B 30% outage, 6-week repair backlog, 5-day SLA, two 25-person cars vs ~300-person surge → single-car ≥12 loads ≈ 6–8 min) sat unread in data the brief supplied. The routed pass ran m019+m021 with m003/m007 gates: the trap style was routed out of top-3 entirely, so no empathy theater ran; the baseline's single genuine insight (residents want the truth about Car B) arrived as a byproduct of theater, while the v6 pass made it a first-class output.
signals.learning_signal: On guarantee/maximize signatures with engineering domains, user-empathy passes must be subordinate to constraint arithmetic — no UX change adds a car; a design cycle that never reads the ops logs is theater. The router's trigger design (trap style out of top-3 when g:estimate/guarantee/maximize) is the protective mechanism that converted this from a loss into a non-loss.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the router's trap-avoidance verified on this signature (m027 triggers fire only on g:decide); add an explicit constraint-before-preference gate (P5 hard-constraint screen) to any style whose registry weakness is constraint-blindness; route truthful-status-type insights through the insight pass (S2) so the human's byproduct insight becomes a mandatory output.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline executed the full design cycle (empathize → define → ideate → prototype → test → iterate) at near-ideal depth — v1 latch failure 4/5, v2 retest 5/5 — and the routed v6 pass matched it move-for-move via the m027 completion contract, which the non-routed v5 run had failed (it selected the strip untested and logged latch ergonomics as an open risk its AAR admitted only testing could resolve). Residual gap: the human's narrative compression (insight density per line) still exceeds the packet's, and the human's watch-based empathy phrasing remains more vivid; the AI's dual-route m025 option framing added pilot go/no-go pricing the human never made explicit.
signals.learning_signal: On user-centered product tasks (product/decide signatures), the empathize step must treat the stated need as an interested-party artifact: run a P1 provenance audit on the survey itself (who benefits from the stated solution; does the instrument pre-assume a product category), and let observation-vs-stated-preference conflict resolution decide the need — the highest-value move is the contradiction, not the survey.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m027 design-cycle as a first-class completion contract on product/decide signatures — prototype, test with real users, and iterate are mandatory outputs, never optional (the v5 run's single biggest loss cause); extend the P1 audit to the need-source; pair with m025 real-options whenever the deliverable is a pilot go/no-go (caps downside, prices the negative branch).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure lateral baseline applied its frame-break to the wrong kind of frame - it converted the load path (physics + code + insurance) into 'an assumption someone stamped', selected the flashiest break (cable-hang) and discarded the safe creative move (columns-as-features). The v6 routed run never routed the lateral style (trap-avoided): confident=no dual-route m001 (fundamentals + drawings/engineer-note anchor) and m018 (steelmanning, which adjudicated that the creative proposal does not survive its own strongest form) with m019 adversary as synthesis context (render-wins-by-enthusiasm vector, unconsulted insurer/city), the mandatory m007 ruin screen (unpriceable distribution -> reject the ruin-adjacent branch), and the constraint-respecting plan delivered with the $1.9M escalation priced and a written-requirement trigger.
signals.learning_signal: The router's trap-avoidance is the whole win on NEG cases: high_stakes signatures with hard physical/regulatory constraints route to evidence-anchored styles (m001 + m018) under the m007 ruin screen, never to the constraint-ignoring style. Lateral's break is only valuable when the frame is a mental model or convention; the P5 hard/soft constraint classification must run before any assumption-break pass is allowed to select, and the legitimate lateral move on hard-constraint cases is flipping the requirement (written trigger), not the structure.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the trap style out of top-3 on hard-constraint signatures (already 97.2%); require P5 hard/soft classification as the gate before any frame-break selection; add the written-requirement trigger pattern (flip the requirement, not the structure - column-free counts only if someone writes it down with a business case) as the standing legitimate lateral move on hard-constraint cases; record the 'discount is the tell' heuristic (price-without-calculations = render-pricing) as an m019 baseline-risk check.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure lateral baseline broke the frame decisively (wait duration -> waiting experience) but left the break unguarded - no failure branch priced, no constraint screen on the generated options, and the gate rested on complaint counts alone. The v6 routed run closed the v5 loss (frame accepted unexamined) with the m028 assumption-break pass as a first-class move, then hardened it: a P1 metric-vs-goal audit (the renewal survey asks about 'elevator experience', so complaints are already the answer to a perception question), a post-ideation hard-constraint screen (capacity, safety, capital), a ranked 8-category inversion gate, and a ruin comparison ($150K bounded worst case vs $4.2M unhedged, dual-metric gate) that the human's one-pass trace did not supply.
signals.learning_signal: On home-turf creative cases the lateral assumption-break pass wins when paired with post-ideation guards: the P5 hard-constraint screen (run AFTER generation, so it never chokes ideation), the m003 inversion gate (R4 on guarantee goals) and the m007 ruin screen (R3 on high_stakes) convert a brilliant reframe into a checkable recommendation - the frame-break is the value, the guards are the safety. The v5 loss (frame accepted) is closed by installing the break as a pass with a completion contract; the residual risk shifts to the break itself going unguarded, which the same guards now cover.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m028 top-1 on high_stakes creative/experience signatures (confident=yes single route is right here); make the post-ideation hard-constraint screen and the dual-metric gate (complaints + sensor, not complaints alone) standing contract items of the m028 pass; record the metric-vs-goal check (P7-style: what does the success metric actually measure?) as a mandatory P1 line on perception-flavored cases.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the strict-combinatorial baseline produced the registry-predicted trap — 18 recombinations of the TMU element space, most off the causal path, with the true fix (remote probe into return air + 0.5C hysteresis + 10-min confirmation delay, ~$500) buried unweighted at position 3 and selection-by-novelty picking a $12k cloud bundle that blows the $3k budget and 3-week timeline. The v6 route held m029 out of top-3 on this signature (the NEG lesson is installed in the router) and ran m031+m044: hypothesis with the supplied data as the discriminating experiment (9/9 ducted-probe units silent), stakeholder screens with recorded reject reasons per option, and the m003 inversion gate enumerating how the fix itself fails. Residual gap: the causal claim remains correlational until the 14-night read; a co-occurring hardware fault is detect-only.
signals.learning_signal: When the element space is small and well-known (a TMU), recombination volume re-circulates non-causal variants and novelty-based selection systematically favors the flashiest option over the working fix — the router must hold the style out of the route and install diagnosis-first (hypothesis + the natural control group already present in the data) with a hard constraint screen (budget/timeline/certification, one reject reason per option); the correct selection then falls out as the single survivor of both screens, with a numeric verification target and escalation rule.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the m029-out-of-top-3 routing for small-element-space diagnose signatures (already learned); generalize the 'free randomized experiment in the supplied data' move (the 9 silent ducted units as a control group) into the m031 contract as a standing check — look for a natural control group before designing any new test; require a numeric verification target + escalation rule in the packet for every guarantee-goal fix, and record a reject reason for every option screened against budget/timeline/certification.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline's win was process, not content — its 12-element inventory and per-recombination viability screen surfaced the non-obvious recombinations (clay-pot thermal mass, low-temp/power-fail alarm circuit, battery depth-of-discharge reserve) that the non-routed v5 AI reached only by convergence. The v6 dual-route (m029+m031) installed that process as the m029 completion contract and matched it first-class, adding the m031 discriminating trial and the m003 inversion-derived safety chain. Residual gap: duty cycle (45-55%) and solar yield remain unmeasured until the field trial — the trial is the only arbiter of the DoD-margin and recharge claims, so the design's error bound stays +-20% until it runs.
signals.learning_signal: On design tasks with an explicit element space, the element-recombination pass is both a completeness AND a filtering engine: enumerating >=8 elements first is what makes non-obvious combinations reachable (headlight-as-heater, thermal mass, alarm topology, battery reserve), and screening each of >=10 recombinations on real numbers (installed wattage >= 2x load, battery Ah x outage with DoD reserve, recharge math, safety chain, cost, serviceability) is what prevents volume from decaying into noise — the filter must run per candidate, not once at selection.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m029 dual-route on design/diagnose signatures with an element list; make the per-recombination viability screen a standing m029 contract item (each of the >=10 recombinations gets a numeric pass/fail with its reason); pair the pass with m031's discriminating field trial as arbiter for unmeasured parameters (duty cycle, DoD, solar yield); retain the m003 inversion gate on guarantee goals so the safety chain is derived from 'how does this kill/fail' rather than from the parts list.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline fell into constraint-worship exactly as the registry predicts (rule = fixed context; beautiful 5,000-LOC stdlib stack; explicit refusal to question the rule), while the v6 route holds the trap style out of top-3 (the learned NEG lesson is installed), dual-routes m063 (multi-party: the approved dependency list is a standing exception, waiver is pre-approved) and m064 (the conflict dissolves on the cost table — pin + re-audit preserves the audit intent), and runs the P5 hard/soft screen FIRST with compliance priced (6 person-months + hand-rolled auth) vs removal (2 days + one waiver) against the binding deadline. Residual gap: the dual-route synthesis costs one reconciliation step the decision itself does not need (all passes agree), and the C' fallback's auth path still depends on a security sign-off if the waiver were denied — detect-and-escalate, not resolved.
signals.learning_signal: An owned, waivable, outdated rule is a parameter to test, not a fence: classify constraints hard vs soft FIRST (origin, owner, waiver path, cost of compliance vs cost of removal), and when removal dominates, escalate the waiver and replace the blunt rule with a precise one (one pinned, audited, vendored dependency; re-audit on CVE) that preserves the original intent. 'Creative within the rule' is how constraint-worship manufactures elaborate wrongness; on deadline signatures the ruin screen must compare floors — ship on deadline with audited auth vs a 100%-capacity custom stack with a hand-rolled auth tail.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the learned routing that holds m030 out of top-3 on decide/high_stakes signatures with a policy rule present; install the P5 hard/soft constraint screen plus an owner/waiver audit (origin, owner, waiver path, compliance-vs-removal cost table required before HOW) as a WHAT gate for any signature containing a stated 'non-negotiable' rule; and extend the m007 ruin screen on deadline+high_stakes signatures to always price the denied-request fallback branch with a named floor deliverable.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 human baseline's home-turf moves — constraint-to-principle conversion ('the only thing that pulls is the rubber band'), the iterative tightening pass, band pre-tension, exact budget discipline — are now produced first-class by the routed m030 pass (hard/soft classification FIRST, deliberate severe-constraint solution, constraint-compatibility check on output, constraint-augmentation iteration), closing the v5 AI's admitted gap (it complied but never tightened) and flipping the verdict from human 4.6/4.4 to AI 4.9/4.6. The m003 inversion gate adds 6 ranked failure categories and the m007 ruin screen adds a probe-gated floor (100 g step) the baseline asserted away. Residual gap: physical capacity stays ±50% (unmeasured material properties) until the 3-step test runs — the design is APPROXIMATED, not SOLVED; the baseline's asserted margin is never tested either, so this is a shared, not a losing, gap.
signals.learning_signal: On severe-constraint design tasks the winning move is not compliance — it is treating the constraint list as a generative operator and then iteratively tightening it: inventory constraints, convert each into a design principle (no cutting → joints are load-bearing; bending unavailable → axial-only; only the band pulls → band lashings), kill the naive candidate on numbers (deck ≈ 40–80 g < 200 g), then re-impose stricter self-constraints (every kit element earns its role, tape caps, exact symmetry) and re-run once. Comply-and-stop produces sound but unrefined designs; the tightening iteration is where margin and elegance come from.
signals.suggested_improvement: Make the m030 contract (hard/soft classification FIRST + deliberate severe-constraint solution + constraint-compatibility check on the output) a standing pass for design signatures with a binding kit list, and move the constraint-augmentation iteration (>=2 stricter self-constraints forcing >=1 refinement) inside the pass so tightening happens in the contract, not as a REVIEW afterthought; pair with the m003 inversion gate so failure structure (joint peel, buckling, sway) is derived before the spec is fixed, and keep the 3-step load protocol as the packet's arbiter for ±50% physical estimates.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline's only salvageable move — 'the nulls are only as good as the instruments' (instrumentation-drift hypothesis) — is absorbed as H5 with a 1-minute independent sampler; everywhere else the routed run diverges exactly where the baseline fails: the baseline's confirm-before-act protocol cost ~$13k per test under a $40k/hr burn and its dashboard-scoped hypothesis space never saw the outbound layer, while the dual-route pass (probe-sense-respond + tempo) widened the frame in 1 minute, found the T-2h geo-fence job, acted reversibly, and verified by recovery curve.
signals.learning_signal: On decide/deadline signatures with a burn rate, confirm-before-act is a purchase order, not a principle: each in-service test costs ~20 min of burn, so the first probe must target outside the current frame (outbound layer, non-deploy changes); three clean nulls inside the modeled space are frame-failure evidence, not eliminations; and any mitigation must carry a pre-registered post-action test so action is an experiment, not a reflex.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m015+m021 dual-route (confident=no) with m028 as context on burn-rate signatures; add the freeze/control-scope audit to P1 (what the freeze does and does not cover); keep the failure branch priced before DO (wrong-kill cost ≈ 5 min) and the 1-minute out-of-frame probe as the standing first move under a burn.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline's winning moves (14:02-vs-14:00 timing tell as a first-class falsifier, information-per-unit-cost test ordering, same-window control split, explicit update ledger) are now mandatory contract outputs of the routed experiment-design pass; the pass adds the window-budget argument (a 20-min APM profile cannot complete inside a 4-min window, so the 2-min probe is the only complete test), an m003 inversion gate (8 ranked failure categories), and a pre-registered next-window falsifier — closing the v5 AI's depth, efficiency and insight gaps against this baseline.
signals.learning_signal: On diagnose/deadline signatures with a windowed phenomenon, the scientific-method pass must treat the phenomenon's own time window as the experiment budget — a test longer than the window is not 'more thorough', it is incomplete; the folklore/anchor input is an interested-party provenance item to audit (P1), and a measured timing offset between anchor and data is a first-class falsifier, not a curiosity.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m031 single-route (confident=yes) with the m003 inversion gate on windowed-diagnosis signatures; add 'test time <= window length' as a standing completion-contract line; keep pre-registered post-fix falsifiers as a packet item so every fix is itself an experiment.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style was nihilistic exactly as registered — it demanded a single decisive falsifier for 'CO2 is the dominant cause of warming,' found none in a noisy system, discounted the accumulated likelihood-ratio evidence (fingerprint sign pattern, <1% vs ~100% attribution) as 'mere corroboration,' refused to quantify belief, and left the policymaker with no position (2.9). The routed v6 pass avoided the trap by construction: the router kept the trap style out of the top-3 and routed to m003+m011, whose completion contracts delivered the pattern-level falsification — ranked failure categories with an un-mitigable residual and never/always rules (m003), and stocks/flows/loops with a falsifying observable (m011: stratospheric warming 5+ yr, decade plateau under rising CO2, fingerprint failure in re-analysis) — plus P3 branch-completeness showing deferral is itself a decision. Verdict: 'yes, dominant, ~95%, with exit conditions' (4.9).
signals.learning_signal: For probabilistic claims, demanding a single decisive falsifier is the error — it is nihilism, not rigor. Falsifiability must be preserved at the pattern level: (1) name the discriminating observation the evidence would have had to show to refute the claim (the opposite fingerprint sign pattern); (2) convert evidence into likelihood ratios rather than confirm/falsify verdicts; (3) pre-commit 2-3 observable downgrade triggers with the confidence drop each would cause — a claim with declared exit conditions is falsifiable in spirit when no single observation can settle it; a claim whose believers cannot name what would weaken it is the unfalsifiable one.
signals.suggested_improvement: On predict-goals with probabilistic evidence, the completion contract for the routed predictive style must include the commitment contract: likelihood ratio of top hypothesis vs best alternative, the discriminating pattern that would refute, and 2-3 pre-registered downgrade triggers emitted as a decision-packet field ('falsification_conditions') so every confident conclusion ships with its exit conditions; inability to state downgrade triggers is a red flag equivalent to unfalsifiability. Keep trap-style exclusion on noisy-attribution signatures (route to inversion+systems, not the pure falsifier style).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human demanded the falsifier as the opening, single instrument ('name the observation that would prove AuraSync false'), demonstrated the claim is a prediction-proof net, and wielded the asymmetry of verification to discard all 4,000 testimonials and the vendor's circular instrument. The non-routed v5 AI reached the identical verdict but buried the falsifier audit inside WHY as one of several checks, so decisiveness arrived late and the risk-free-confirmation principle was never stated. The routed v6 pass (m001+m032 dual-route) made the falsifier-first move the opening instrument with an objective completion contract — falsifier stated per claim, disconfirming test designed first, unfalsifiable claims rejected, probabilistic claims reformulated with pre-registered ranges — and added the m001 order-of-magnitude physics kill (7.83 Hz ≈ 10^-8 K vs kT) plus the m044 stakeholder frame, closing both gaps; only raw step-count efficiency still favors the human monologue.
signals.learning_signal: The falsifiability test is not one check among many: on claims that 'look scientific' (mechanism jargon, testimonials, self-made instruments) it is the decisive instrument and must be the opening move with a completion contract — falsifier per claim, prediction-proof-net check (if every possible outcome is absorbable, the claim is unfalsifiable as stated and must be reformulated into a risky form before funding), and an evidence-weight audit scoring each item by the risk it took (risk-free confirmations weigh zero — the asymmetry of verification). The vendor's willingness to be put at risk is itself evidence: refusal to accept a sham-controlled design is an answer.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m001+m032 dual-route on vendor-claims/decision signatures (R2 pair); make the falsifier-first pass a standing completion contract on any claim with mechanism jargon or testimonial evidence (falsifier per sub-claim, disconfirming test designed FIRST, unfalsifiable claims rejected, probabilistic claims handled as ranges with pre-registered thresholds — never nihilism); record the risk-acceptance test (claimant's willingness to be put at risk) as a decision-packet field.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style proposed a powered-but-infeasible 9-week reverse-rollback (n ~41,200/arm) for a 2-week board deadline - template rigidity + ecological-validity gap - and rejected the quasi-experimental evidence entirely. The routed run interrogated every claim's provenance first (m094: CFO claim, self-selected survey, before/after all labeled interested-party or confounded), applied m035/m037 robustness and competence boundary, and priced the deck's one-shot risk with an m007 distribution + floor + decline/restructure branch. Vs the v5 AI: same conclusion, but the merchant-dashboard comparator was found FIRST pass instead of after the broken-RCT detour.
signals.learning_signal: On irreversible-global-rollout attribution with a deadline, route to source-interrogation FIRST (m094) with the m007 one-shot ruin screen as the gate: 'claim provenance before design' names the natural placebo (untouched comparator line) before any design is drawn and forces a decline/restructure branch instead of rigor theater.
signals.suggested_improvement: Install 'claim provenance before design' + the m007 one-shot/ruin screen as standing gates on any attribution-with-deadline task (NEG win held at ~4.9); pre-analyze available comparison populations in WHAT; keep routing AWAY from m033 on NEG signatures (template rigidity), consistent with 97.2% router trap-avoidance.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline solved the power x timeline conflict as a design input and audited the finance bar against the economics ($6.70/activation); the v5 AI discovered both only at verification/REVIEW and patched them. The routed m033 pass (completion contract: intervention/control/randomization/blinding/exact outcome measure/power-effect-size check/ecological-validity note) made both first-class HOW outputs, and the P1 provenance audit converted the interested-party bar into a derived, checked threshold. Baseline's residual edge is nil; AI wins narrowly on contract completeness (8-category inversion gate, ecological-validity note, uncertainty ledger).
signals.learning_signal: On design-with-deadline tasks the m033 completion contract converts REVIEW-stage patches into design inputs: horizon-vs-budget is solved jointly inside the pass (day-30 8,400/arm = 50d > 42d -> pre-registered day-14 surrogate primary 5,300/arm = ~27d), and interested-party bars are re-derived, not inherited. The surrogate-primary move generalizes to any long-outcome experiment under a budget.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m033 + contract on decide/estimate/deadline signatures (POS win confirmed); add 'convert interested-party thresholds via the same arithmetic before inheriting them' (P1) as a standing item on all threshold-driven designs; keep the workspace-cluster sensitivity check as the B2B ecological-validity default.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline defined the construct AS the contractual metric ('the construct for decision purposes is the claims-based rate'), verified the drop at ~5.5 standard errors, and recommended RENEW — the canonical measures-the-measurable-not-the-important failure — while the routed run caught it structurally: the R3-mandatory adversary pass enumerated the gaming vectors with quantified exposure (observation stays +500/yr, ER-return-without-admission +400/yr = 4.5x headroom for the 200 missing patients), the evidence-weighted SWOT graded the headline as strong evidence for the indicator but no evidence for the construct, and the de-gamed renewal plan (audit-based metric, frozen definition, guardrail caps, renegotiation) came out of the institution-design view. Residual gap: the audit CI (14.9-16.3) leaves up to ~1 pp of genuine improvement indistinguishable from zero, and the 6-month renegotiation window is the binding constraint.
signals.learning_signal: When a metric is the explicit target of incentives, the metric is a map under attack — cases must go somewhere, so read the ledger's neighbors (observation stays, exclusions, definitional migrations) and triangulate with an instrument produced OUTSIDE the incentive path; a statistically overwhelming drop in an incentivized metric (5.5 SE) is a red flag, not evidence, when an independent instrument shows the construct flat. The adversary pass (R3 on adversarial signatures) makes leakage enumeration, capacity checking (missing cases vs substitution-channel headroom), and unconsulted-stakeholder listing mandatory rather than emergent, and the P7 audit must distinguish indicator-validity from construct-validity: a perfectly audited indicator can still measure the wrong thing.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the R3 m019 gate on adversarial signatures with the quantified-exposure contract; add a mandatory capacity-check sub-step — count the missing cases and compare against the substitution channels' headroom before accepting any incentivized-metric drop; extend the P7 audit to output which instruments are produced outside the incentive path and record that split in the packet's provenance section; on adversarial signatures with metric-driven pay, pair the adversary pass with an institution-design view so the de-gamed alternative is priced, not just named.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline was near-gold (construct decomposition first, instrument audit before reading any number, inline sensitivity bound), and the routed measurement pass now matches it first-class while closing the v5 AI's two gaps by contract: construct decomposition + instrument audit land in WHAT before any comparison (the non-routed v5 AI reached them only as a hypothesis in WHY), and sensitivity is priced at breakeven (B's clone share must fall from 55% to <= 26.7% — a 28-pp misspecification — to flip the verdict) plus ~12-sigma sampling gap instead of a terse note. Residual gap: clone shares are the instrumentation team's estimates (interested-party — B's designers benefit from B shipping); no independent verification channel exists in-scope, and the re-run is the only real fix.
signals.learning_signal: Measurement precedes reading: before comparing any two numbers, audit the instrument's semantic fidelity — what event fires, under what trigger, whether it can fire without the construct — because a corrupted event inverts verdicts (naive +3 pp becomes corrected -10.2 pp) while the data stay identical. The routed m034 pass (operational definition with exact measure/instrument/units, P7 measurement-validity/Goodhart audit, measures-the-measurable-not-the-important check) makes this the first-class WHAT move, and the R4 m003 inversion gate generalizes it into a ranked enumeration of how the experiment could be made to ship the worse arm — the leakage is the top category, realized.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep dual-route m033+m034 first-class on signatures with undefined constructs + metric-driven decide/goals (P7 already hard-wired in WHY); extend the measurement-pass checklist with (a) a breakeven threshold — the parameter value at which the verdict flips, stated as distance from the reported estimate — and (b) an interested-party flag on instrument estimates (who built the instrument, who benefits from the verdict); attach the inversion gate's 'how the worse arm ships' category list as the instrument audit's test plan.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style's reflex was variance-side — it pre-registered a 12-week, $40k second-vendor replication (samples, settings, methods, definitions, windows) and deferred the launch decision past the seasonal dip and into the competitor's window, never auditing the measurement layer: client-side telemetry drops 31% of sessions (Android 13+ background limits, ad-blockers), missingness correlates with the churn-prone users the feature targets, and the second vendor's SDK is the same client-side class, so the replication faithfully reproduces the blind spot. The routed v6 run won WHILE running the router's pick (m094, top-1 — the router keeps the trap style out of top-3): the first-class pass interrogated the null claim's evidence basis (a null on 69% of sessions, missing not at random) and the replication proposal's premise (replication is a variance remedy, never a bias remedy); the m006 gate (unmeasured) produced likelihood scenarios whose range spans the ship threshold (threshold flip demonstrated); the m019 gate (adversarial) priced the ritual's cost against the window (12 w / $40k vs 2 w, out-of-window vs in-window). Selected: instrument repair + backfill re-analysis of the SAME study, decision in ~2 weeks, both corrected outcomes pre-planned. Residual gap: backfill data quality (±0.3 pp) is named but not priceable until the backfill runs.
signals.learning_signal: Robustness checks validate the measurement layer before the variance layer: before demanding more samples, settings, or vendors, run a coverage/missingness audit (what fraction of the population did the instrument see, and is the missingness non-random?) and a bias-vs-variance classification of the threat — replication repairs variance, never bias; a replica of a biased instrument reproduces the bias at multiplied cost, so when bias is plausible the correct move is instrument repair + re-measurement of the SAME cohort, and the cost of delay (decision windows, competitor clocks, seasonal dips) belongs IN the alternative table. For null results specifically: a null computed on a non-randomly missing subset is a finding about the instrument, not about the treatment — absence of measurement is not evidence of absence. The router's trap-avoidance pattern (NEG top-1 away from trap style, 97.2%) is what lets the agent hold the protective split while the style is installed — the trap's moves become gate-checks (measurement-validity before replication), not commands.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m094 as the confident single-route first-class pass for this signature (decide/estimate/maximize + adversarial,deadline,unmeasured) — the critical-reading contract should require interrogating every decision-relevant claim's evidence basis (what does it assert, on what was measured, does the instrument see the population it claims to measure?) and every proposed remedy's premise (would the remedy's instrument see what the original missed?); add a 'coverage/missingness audit' item to the m006 gate: missingness rate + mechanism + non-randomness test, run before any NEEDS_EVIDENCE/replication demand is accepted; add a 'ritual-cost' item to the m019 gate: any delay/replication option must be priced against the earliest binding decision deadline and the baseline risk of inaction; keep tempo mode (P2) so the repair path commits at DO.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 non-routed run stopped at instability — it correctly blocked the rollout but commissioned a fresh 2-week experiment to 'separate signal from artifact,' while the human's decisive check (definition invariance: recompute the outcome under an alternative operationalization computable from the held clickstream) overturned the result outright (+0.2 pp, n.s.) and named the mechanism (auto-completed tutorial inflating Flow B's activation, concentrated in paid-search). The routed v6 run closed that gap: the m035 first-class pass made the definition-invariance check a mandatory HOW output (completion contract: replication conditions named, >=2 P4 robustness perturbations, artifact-vs-effect discrimination), so the artifact is found in existing data and the new-experiment alternative is suppressed by the P3 gate (no new-data alternative while a held-data check is available); the dual-route m094 pass additionally exposed that the two arms measured different constructs (tap-counted vs quiz-graded tutorial completion — an instrument difference, not a behavior difference), and the m007 ruin screen (R3, high_stakes) priced the ship-artifact downside (phantom adoption, re-rollout, trust loss). Residual shared gap: clickstream reflects true behavior is an assumption, not verified — a future test should instrument both definitions simultaneously in one arm.
signals.learning_signal: When a robustness battery overturns a single result, the decisive check is the definitional one — recompute the outcome under at least 2 alternative operationalizations computable from data already held, and run this BEFORE any new-data alternative (a gate, not a suggestion): significance tests validate a fixed metric, never the metric's construct. Deeper: before interpreting any difference between two arms, verify instrument equivalence — if the arms' instruments operationalize the same labeled metric differently (auto-complete vs quiz-graded completion), the comparison is between instruments, not behaviors, and statistics on it are arithmetic about the instruments. Artifact-vs-effect discrimination is the pass's terminal output: name the mechanism, show it is concentrated where it is (segment × definition), and state the conditions under which a future result would be trusted.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m035 as a dual-routed first-class pass on this signature (decide/maximize + deadline/high_stakes) with the full completion contract: replication-conditions named (settings/samples/methods variations), >=2 P4 perturbations (segment, definition, window) with recomposition arithmetic, artifact-vs-effect discrimination, and trust conditions; add an 'instrument-equivalence check' item to the m035 contract — verify both arms' instruments measure the same construct before interpreting any difference; keep the P3 gate 'no new-data alternative while a definition-invariance check on held data is available' as a packet line; keep m007 as standing R3 gate for high_stakes rollout signatures (ship-vs-hold downside distribution).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline failed on its registered weakness — seven equal-weight models, a multi-front fight plan, the dominant fact (the account is lost) buried as one bullet. The routed run treated the multi-model pass as a convergence check: m063 (each party's interests, incl. the buyer's disruption-avoidance during a consolidation year) and m064 (accountability to employees and reference integrity) both pointed the same way, and the m019/m003/m007 gates priced every defensive option unaffordable on the margin math (30% below on an 8% margin; $3.6M = 45% of revenue vs $7.3M breakeven) — so the simple transition answer (phase-out negotiation using the zero-disruption asset + replacement for $3.6M + workforce options with T-30 triggers) became the headline, exactly the closure the strict human baseline refused. Residual shared gap: the buyer-reversal probability is a base-rate estimate (stated intent + price gap + savings mandate), not measured; both plans depend on it only at the margin.
signals.learning_signal: The latticework is a blind-spot reducer, not a truth generator: when the routed passes and gates all converge on one direction, the pass must CLOSE — convergence detection (all weighted factors point one way → state the simple conclusion and use remaining factors only for contradiction checks, never to generate alternatives) is the anti-model-soup mechanism; fight/defend alternatives must fail a cost-based falsification (margin vs. gap computed before survival) and the ruin floor makes the transition the only non-ruin branch, so a 6+ model matrix with hedged recommendations and the simple answer buried should score below.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m063+m064 dual-route on consolidate-and-cut signatures (router confident=no; m019 doubles as gate and synthesis context); install the convergence check (>=80% of weighted factors same direction → close) as a standing WHY/HOW boundary item; keep tempo mode (P2) on 3-month deadlines so the transition commits at DO with triggers, and the negotiation asset (zero-disruption service) is spent inside the window; generalize the ruin-floor rule: any alternative whose failure cost exceeds the survival floor on the base rate must be priced before DO.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline's strength was a deliberate cross-disciplinary pass whose intersection constrained the plan before selection — the routed run now reproduces it as a first-class HOW pass: all five binding implications (procurement tender gate + new-ARR-only comp principal-agent, grandfather-clause exit, GPU capacity bottleneck, Red Queen parity clock + selective cull, compounding EV check) are produced as contract outputs before selection, closing the two moves the non-routed v5 AI surfaced only at REVIEW (the no-discount-retention cull and the parity-clock front-load). The routed run adds what the human lacked: evidence-weighted grading of the board's own proposal (m070), quantified adversary exposure on the $28M Legacy block (m019), and six ranked inversion failure categories including the capacity-churn branch (m003). Residual shared gap: the softest numbers (tender-trigger probability at $50K; true Scale elasticity) are unmeasured; both sides defer measurement to Q1 and both plans are robust to them.
signals.learning_signal: A cross-disciplinary inventory is a first-class pass, not an afterthought: on decide/guarantee + adversarial pricing signatures, running >=4 named disciplines (incentives, psychology, rate-limits, competition), each required to produce one binding implication from scenario evidence, then taking the INTERSECTION of their demands (not the union), changes which constraints bind before selection — the parity clock and the low-fitness cull are invisible to hypothesis-evidence routing because no stage asks 'which discipline's constraint could bind here?'. Completion contract: each model must change the plan or the pass is incomplete; the synthesis must be a single segmented plan satisfying every implication, never a list of independent demands.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m036+m070 dual-route on this signature (router confident=no); make 'intersection, not union' and 'each model must change the plan' standing m036 contract items; retain m003/m019 as the guarantee/adversarial gates (they priced the uniform-raise failure branch before DO); add board-proposal-as-claim grading (evidence-weighted SWOT) as a standing HOW item on any pricing/strategy board decision; measure the softest numbers in Q1 before the Scale steps land.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline's honest refusal is locally correct and globally destructive — it collapsed 'I cannot execute ML' into 'I cannot lead ML' (role-collapse category error) and its learn-first stance forfeits the 24-month window. The v6 AI's routed pre-commitment pass converts the competence gap into a delegation-with-verification contract and prices the decline (12-month drift = half the window) before the boundary is invoked.
signals.learning_signal: On adversarial/deadline signatures, a pure competence-boundary stance degrades into refusal unless gated by (1) execution-vs-orchestration role decomposition, (2) a priced decline option, (3) a pre-committed verification structure with a named technical authority and a graded exit.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep m088 pre-commitment as top-1 for this signature (router already holds it there); make 'decline priced as a decision' and 'delegation with named authority + checkpoint exit' standing outputs of any competence-adjacent pass; never let 'I can't execute X' decide 'I can't lead X'.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline drew the boundary and refused the unvalidatable rate in one pass; the v6 AI reached the same allocation only through routed structure (boundary pass + ruin screen + threshold flip p* = 17.5%) — the exact structure the non-routed v5 run lacked (it committed $1.5M direct on the deck's rate, realized 0.6x down-round). Residual baseline edge: it priced the delegation with realized-history humility in one line; the routed pass needed its full gate stack to get there.
signals.learning_signal: On decide/estimate signatures with finance/medical domains, the load-bearing-probability check (who certifies p, EV threshold flip, sensitivity to a corrected class rate) is what converts a competence boundary from narrative into a gate; a boundary pass without the threshold flip still lets a fluent EV win.
signals.suggested_improvement: Standing module on high_stakes decide/estimate tasks: force (1) provenance of the load-bearing probability, (2) its EV threshold flip, (3) the delegation price, before any EV is trusted; pair with the m007 ruin screen (full distribution + floor + one-shot).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-margin human baseline declined to bid on a blanket 2× margin ($1.04M cost basis, ≈ 24-week schedule) against a contract whose true tail is ±20% (reference class, 90% of cases; worst plausible $660k/11.5 wk) and whose downside is contractually capped at ≈ $80–120k — forgoing ≈ $165k now and ≈ $2M/5yr of repeat + vendor-list business to 'avoid' a capped $120k loss. The non-routed v5 AI escaped by calibrating ($700k/11.5 wk), but the routed run makes the escape structural: the m038 contract's over-conservatism check + derating (2× → ≈ 17% cost margin + 2-wk schedule buffer) gate-checks the style's own failure mode in-frame, the m007 ruin screen proves no ruin path (max loss $120k < $165k expected profit — the cap is the true ruin bound), m023 prices the forgone alternative at ≈ $2M/5yr, m019 audits the competitor's under-margined $610k baseline, and m088 pre-commits the delivery buffers. Residual shared gap: cost beyond the ±20% tail (10% of cases) is absorbed by the caps only if the client honors them (litigation risk unmodeled).
signals.learning_signal: On adversarial/high_stakes decide signatures with a contractually capped downside, margin is a derated calibration, not a blanket factor: size it from (a) the reference-class base rate (±20%, 90% of cases), (b) the named-risk worst case ($660k/11.5 wk), and (c) the contract cap as the true ruin bound (≈ $120k). A blanket 2× margin on top of a capped downside is taxed twice — it forfeits an uncapped upside that never needed insuring (≈ 20× overpay: $2M/5yr foregone to avoid ≤ $120k). The derating test: 'does the demanded margin cost more than the risk it retires?' — if yes, derate to evidence-based sizing and pre-commit the buffers that actually win (schedule + scope-change protocol) rather than the one that kills the bid (2× cost).
signals.suggested_improvement: Add to the m038 contract a derating clause: when the downside is contractually capped, (1) compute the true ruin bound from the contract (exit clause, penalty cap) and compare it against the uncapped upside (repeat contracts, market entry) before choosing any factor, (2) derive the margin from the reference class (m097) + named-risk worst case instead of a blanket multiplier, (3) run the 'margin costs more than the risk' test (m023) and derate if positive, (4) convert the freed margin into pre-committed operational buffers (m088: schedule slack, scope-change protocol). Extend the m007 ruin-screen ordering: on capped-loss contracts the floor/Kelly line becomes a cap-vs-upside asymmetry check, and the ruin question is 'can the contract lose us more than X?', not 'what is the worst statistical case?'

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the human's decisive move was cushioning the binding n=1 uncertainty (surge factor — a single non-instrumented observation, ±25%) to reach 115 kN/m², and the non-routed v5 AI lost exactly there: it priced the one-sided tail against a $230k premium on EV grounds (1% × $3.5M = $35k < $230k), chose 92 kN/m², and the graded 93 kN/m² event damaged it (plate yield ≈ $340k). The routed run converts the human's winning move into load-bearing structure: the m038 contract's margin-quantified flip-point table (92 flips at any single-factor ≈ 2σ miss; 115 flips only at a joint miss), the P1 provenance audit (surge = n=1 observation adverse to the cheap option — the tell it is real), the m003 inversion gate (6 ranked failure categories), and P3 pricing the 92-failure branch ($340k–3.5M). Residual shared gap: tourism growth +60% and the ±25% surge bound are asserted, not measured; the wind-event coincidence is unmodeled.
signals.learning_signal: On estimate/guarantee signatures whose margin chain contains a single-observation (n=1) error factor, EV arithmetic systematically underweights the one-sided tail: the non-routed run discounted a ~1% joint event against the premium and lost the style's home turf. The margin-quantified contract — 'how wrong must each estimate be before the decision flips?' — makes the binding factor the sizing object: the design must cover the error in the margin's own inputs, not just the nominal numbers, and a one-sided error structure (a survey can only understate) earns a one-sided margin. The cushion is then priced against the failure it retires (92→115 costs $230k vs a $340k–3.5M tail — the cheapest item in the budget), not EV-discounted as a premium.
signals.suggested_improvement: Install the m038 first-class contract as: (1) margin-quantified — a per-factor flip-point table ('how wrong before the decision flips'), (2) binding-uncertainty audit — n=1 / single-observation factors get the cushion instead of a sensitivity note, with a P1 who-benefits check (a factor adverse to the cheap option is the tell it is real), (3) over-conservatism check — opportunity cost of the cushion priced against the failure it retires, (4) derating — factors backed by evidence are not inflated; reserve the over-conservatism gate for capped-downside cases. Pair with the m003 inversion gate on guarantee goals (ranked failure categories before selection) and P3 (price the under-cushioned branch before DO).

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the style-pure human baseline failed every precondition audit — it treated the mandatory year-2 +$200k follow-on as a voluntary top-up (true max loss $500k/−25%, not the labeled −15%), absorbed a tail at 1.8× fair value (slot EV −50%) as 'the price of a lottery ticket', misclassified the ladder (bounded, priced, positively skewed, zero-ruin, duration-matched) as 'the forbidden middle', and selected B at −3.7% EV with the worse worst case; the non-routed v5 AI already caught the trap (contract audit at framing, EV(B) −73,500, worst −25%, decision M). The routed run made the trap-catch structural: the router de-routes m039 on this signature (KB trap record 2.0/5.0) and dual-routes steelman + red team, whose divergence triggers P3 branch-completeness and P4 calibration — the break-even threshold p(5×) = 0.149 (seller's 10% claim sits a third below the indifference point) is a new non-obvious number the v5 traces lacked. Residual shared gap: B's 10% probability is the seller's unverifiable claim; M's 0.3% credit event is small-sample, priced by spread.
signals.learning_signal: Barbell preconditions are falsifiable contract facts, not labels: optionality means reading the clause (mandatory follow-on ⇒ not optional; the true cap is 25%, not the labeled 15%), cheapness means premium vs actuarial fair value (1.8× ⇒ tail-hostile; tail slot EV −50%), and 'the middle' means a genuinely negative-skew, ruin-prone bet — a bounded, priced, positively skewed, zero-ruin asset (the ladder) is the safe core extended, not the forbidden middle. On high_stakes signatures with a convexity product, run the ruin screen and branch-completeness BEFORE any barbell adoption, and compute the break-even probability (EV(B) ≥ 0 ⇒ p(5×) ≥ 0.149 vs the seller's 0.10) as a standard line — the threshold flip is the cheapest detector of an overpriced tail.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the NEG-signature routing as learned (confident=no → m018/m019 dual-route with m028 synthesis; m039 deliberately de-routed on its own trap signature — style-pure barbell scored 2.0/5.0 there): the steelman pass carries the barbell claim and the red team falsifies it with contract facts, and the V3 divergence triggers the P3+P4 resolution. Install 'break-even probability vs stated claim' (p* = cost of tail / 5× payoff net of core) as a mandatory m007 ruin-screen line whenever a structured-note tail is present, and add 'is the middle actually ruinous?' (skew sign + boundedness + ruin prob, not label) to the m039 classification step so the POS-style reasoning inverts correctly when the environment flips tail-hostile.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 human baseline verified all three barbell preconditions in-frame before pricing (cheap — forced sellers ⇒ 60% of fair; optional — capped, no follow-on; survivable — 8% tail < 10% pain cap) and used the ruin/skew ranking to beat the variance trap; the non-routed v5 AI computed every number correctly (EV(M) 57,120, EV(B) 117,400, worst +41,400 vs −300,000, P(loss>20%) 0% vs 4%, SD trap) but treated tail-friendliness as a stated assumption instead of an audited gate, and sized the tail without a survivability bar. The routed run turned the three preconditions into load-bearing in-frame checks (m039 pass contract + P1 who-benefits audit of the cheapness claim + m007 floor/Kelly: tail-slot full-Kelly ≈ 5.8% vs actual 8%, accepted only because capped/survivable) and added the metric-inversion insight, reaching the same 92/8 with the v5 gap closed. Residual shared gap: the forced-seller discount is asserted market fact, not measured; the 70% worthless tail path is an accepted cost of convexity.
signals.learning_signal: On decide/guarantee signatures with a supplied convexity product (high_stakes, finance), the barbell's preconditions are gate checks, not assumptions: cheapness must be provenance-audited (who benefits from the price claim — here the claim is adverse to the seller, the tell of a genuine forced-seller discount), optionality verified in the contract (capped, no margin/roll/follow-on), and survivability sized against an explicit pain cap (tail loss 8% < 10%). Rank asymmetric payoffs on worst case + ruin probability + skew, never on variance: the portfolio with the HIGHER SD (B ≈ 162.9k) is the only one that cannot lose money — low variance is not safety when all the variance sits on the loss side.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the m039 first-class pass contract as: (1) safe-core floor named, (2) optionality read from the contract, (3) cheapness proven by mechanism + who-benefits (forced-seller discounts are the adverse-to-seller price claim — audit it), (4) survivability vs pain cap, (5) middle-bet rejection stated before pricing; pair with the m007 ruin screen's floor/Kelly line (note when Kelly is degenerate — log-utility endorses all-in on any no-wealth-ruin branch — and let the floor/ruin screen override it on one-shot income frames); add the metric-inversion tell ('riskiest-looking by SD is safest by downside') as an insight-pass template for asymmetric-payoff signatures.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style misidentified leverage (its registry weakness) — it ranked a $500k/6-month goals/KPI program above the observed cause (checkout regression from the API upgrade; 1 engineer-hour fix restoring ~$1.2M/month) and dismissed the deployment-window correlation without opening the funnel or deploy data. The v6 router sent no structural-lever style on this adversarial/deadline/unmeasured signature; the m019 adversary pass (baseline-risk comparison attacking the program's unfalsifiable assumptions), the m006 provenance audit (likelihood scenarios showing the deployment hypothesis dominates any honest posterior), and m021 tempo (commit at DO under $40k/day cost-of-delay) caught the trap before ranking. Residual: the leverage-misidentification check is gate-borne rather than module-borne — m040 itself was not routed, so the trap is only closed when the gates fire.
signals.learning_signal: Leverage is defined by change per effort along the observed causal chain, not structural depth: on decide/diagnose signatures with adversarial, deadline, or unmeasured context, route adversary + tempo + provenance (m019/m021/m006) instead of any structural-lever style; an unfalsifiable 'deep' story with no onset-window tie must lose to the cheapest candidate that fully explains the windowed data.
signals.suggested_improvement: Formalize a leverage-misidentification screen as a standing gate wherever a 'deep lever vs direct fix' framing appears: per-candidate falsifiable observable, onset-window tie, and baseline-risk comparison against the cheapest full-explanation candidate; keep m040 out of signatures containing adversarial/deadline/unmeasured triggers (already reflected in the router) and re-verify on this case's regression re-run.

signals.key_gap: vs baseline: both sides converged on the same verdict (2-week incident-to-change-class pipeline + canary rule for the 5 recurring classes; defer the 25 hires; ~30% incident cut, SLO >= 99.9% in 2 quarters), but in v5 the AI reached it late, opening sympathetic to the board's capacity frame and ranking by arithmetic; the v6 routed pass made the human's first-sight advantage a completion contract — loop map + full leverage-scale positioning at HOW entry, change-per-effort ranking, and a per-point falsifiable observable (misidentification check: five-class share must fall within 60 days) that the baseline only implied in one line. Residual human edge: one-pass elegance — the packet + gate machinery is still heavier than the pure single pass.
signals.learning_signal: On org/reliability guarantee signatures the routed leverage pass plus structure-first scan (S1) converts the leverage style's first-sight loop mapping into a mandatory deliverable: map the governing loops before arithmetic, position every candidate on the leverage scale (parameters < delays < negative-feedback strength < information flows < rules < goals), and give each ranked point a falsifiable observable so misidentification is caught by the verification metric itself.
signals.suggested_improvement: Keep the m040-first-class route on guarantee signatures (top3 m040/m031/m070); make the per-point falsifiable-observable a standing m040 contract item; keep the P8 closed-scope fast path on fully-specified recommendation briefs to trim the packet overhead that cost the efficiency dimension.

signals.key_gap: vs the v5 baseline: the pure decomposition style partitioned four simultaneous alerts into four sub-problems and spent 38 minutes on internally consistent per-service checks that could not converge (cause outside every sub-problem's boundary), resolving at T+47 only by luck-assembled pattern overlap. The routed run held the v5 AI win and improved it: the m033 experiment-design pass framed the shared config/deploy diff as the single-variable discriminating experiment (outcome measure = all four alert sets clearing simultaneously), the m091 pass validated the chunk boundary BEFORE executing any runbook chunk (chunks sharing a substrate make chunked execution invalid), the m015 emergence context applied the complicated-vs-complex test (shared substrate → aggregate is emergent → probe, don't plan), and tempo mode (P2) bounded the whole move at T≈15 min with a pre-named escalation floor if the rollback failed. The m003 inversion gate priced the per-service trap itself as the #1 ranked failure category and added the change-control finding (root cause of the root cause).
signals.learning_signal: On multi-symptom deadline problems, decomposition must be GATED on chunk-boundary validity: if symptoms co-occur in time and share a substrate (config/deploy/DB/cache/mesh), the shared-cause hypothesis is tested first and per-symptom work is demoted to a bounded post-fix confirmation sweep. The cheap discriminating experiment (deploy/config diff) is the highest-information first action; the outcome measure is all symptom sets clearing simultaneously, not any single service's dashboard. A chunk-boundary validation step (m091) plus the complicated-vs-complex probe-don't-plan rule (m015) is the decomposition-blindness guard this case is engineered to punish.
signals.suggested_improvement: Install a mandatory cross-cutting scan as the WHAT-stage gate for multi-symptom deadline signatures: (1) check simultaneity and shared substrate before any per-symptom sub-plan; (2) record the one-cause-vs-many hypothesis with its falsifier and order diagnostics by information-per-minute (diff first); (3) require the m033 pass's exact outcome measure (all symptom sets clear) before declaring resolution; (4) keep the m091 chunk-boundary validation as the standing decomposition-blindness guard; (5) log the 'sub-problems pass but the goal is unmet => cause is outside the decomposition' stop rule as a REVIEW check.

signals.key_gap: vs the v5 baseline (which won this case 5.0/4.0 on first-pass coverage, designed critical-path math, and deliberate merge-back): the routed run closed all three gaps the baseline exploited. The m041 completion contract installed the clause-to-stream coverage matrix as a WHAT-stage gate artifact (5/5 goal clauses claimed on the FIRST pass, no second sweep), the critical path with duration + float is computed in design (10 wks + 1 wk float from the enforced wk-7 confirmation deadline), and merge-back (run-of-show, budget roll-up, single source of truth) is a designed first-class component. The m024 regret pass added fail-safe ordering (highest-regret nodes locked first) and the m039 barbell pass added revenue-floor budgeting (safe core funded from the two guaranteed floors; contingency the only unallocated money); the m007 ruin screen converted venue risk from a REVIEW note into a governed wk-4 floor trigger (if P(venue) < 0.85, backup track + restructure) with a decline/restructure alternative named.
signals.learning_signal: On guarantee/predict planning signatures with high stakes, the decomposition family's edge is its MACHINERY, and it must be first-class: clause-to-stream coverage as a gate artifact, leaves with owner class + duration, explicit dependency edges with critical-path duration and float computed in design, and a designed merge-back step. The v5 loss pattern was treating completeness and integration as checks (REVIEW sweeps) instead of design-time artifacts. Regret (m024) and barbell (m039) passes convert the same hierarchy into fail-safe ordering and asymmetric resource allocation; a one-shot ruin screen (m007) adds a governed trigger instead of a narrative risk.
